title: समासः — A Compound-Formation Rule Book
subtitle: Compiled with reference to G. Mahabaleshwara भट्ट's 'समासः' (Samskrita Bharati, Bengaluru), cross-referenced to पाणिनि's अष्टाध्यायी and the लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी of वरदराज
source_note: Rule topics, ordering, and pedagogical examples follow the structure of the source manual 'समासः' by Vidwan G. Mahabaleshwara भट्ट (Samskrita Bharati, 'Aksharam', Bengaluru; ISBN 81-88220-02-7), a study book for Samasa prepared for Samskrita Bharati students. The source states many rules with अष्टाध्यायी सूत्र citations but without expounding their meaning in its own Chapter 2 (examples chapter); fuller सूत्र citations appear in its Chapter 4 (detailed chapter). This JSON restates rule explanations and cross-references independently in our own words, verifies सूत्र numbering against the standard अष्टाध्यायी, and reproduces the source's own worked examples (which are themselves few-word traditional grammatical forms, not the author's original prose) rather than copying explanatory sentences verbatim.

how_to_read.vigraha: विग्रहः — the analytical (expanded) sentence/phrase that the compound resolves into
how_to_read.purvapada / uttarapada: the first member / second (final) member of a compound
how_to_read.pradhana: प्राधान्य — which member's sense is 'dominant' (governs external syntax); this is how the four major समास classes (तत्पुरुष, बहुव्रीहि, dvandva, अव्ययीभाव) are told apart
how_to_read.process: how the compound is formed grammatically per this rule (e.g. vibhakti-lopa = case-ending elision on samasing)

book_structure_note: The source book covers: Ch.1 definitions (samasa/vigraha/bhedah/samasartha, discursive prose), Ch.2 one worked example per subtype (pp.6-16), Ch.3 purva/uttara-pada-specific morphological rules incl. gender and samasanta suffixes (pp.17-33), Ch.4 detailed treatment with sutra citations, subtype by subtype (pp.34-58), Ch.5 cautions (pp.59-63), Ch.6 prakriya/derivation-step walkthroughs (pp.64-67), Ch.7 exercises + answer key (pp.68-82). This rulebook covers Ch.3 and Ch.4 in full -- the technical core of the source -- organized below by the four samasa classes (tatpurusha, bahuvrihi, dvandva, avyayibhava) plus a separate purvapada_uttarapada_rules section for the Ch.3 morphology that cuts across all four. Ch.1 (definitions/theory prose) and Ch.5-7 (cautions, derivation walkthroughs, exercises) are not included, as they are discursive or pedagogical rather than rule-book material; see summary_counts.status for exact coverage.

tatpurusha.english_name: Nominative(-sense) Tatpurusha — 'part/position' words compounded with the whole
tatpurusha.rule: Two sub-rules, both compounding words that stand in the same case (समानाधिकरण, loosely 'nominative-sense') with the noun they qualify: (1) The words पूर्व, apara, adhara, uttara (denoting a portion — front/back/lower/upper part) and ardha (half) compound with a padstem denoting the whole of which they are a part, provided the 'whole' word is singular/one entity. (2) Any word denoting 'a portion' (एकदेशवाची) compounds with a time-word (कालवाची), e.g. madhyama, पूर्व, apara, सायम् + ahan/रात्रि.
tatpurusha.process: अदेश-rahita (no substitution) + vibhakti-lopa on समास — the first word stays in its stem/nominative-sense form and both members' original case endings drop, replaced by the compound's own single ending
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The source's Ch.2 table example for this row is vigraha 'अर्धं ग्रामस्य' → समास 'अर्धग्रामः'. Its own Ch.4 footnote (f, p.35) qualifies this: word order matters — 'ग्रामार्धः' (ग्राम first) would instead be a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, requiring the masculine noun ardha in the vigraha ('ग्रामस्य अर्धः'); only 'ardha-' placed first, as in अर्धपिप्पली below, is this (प्रथमा) type. This nuance is preserved here rather than silently resolved, since it affects how the rule should be worded.

examples.gloss: the front part of the body
the back part of the house
the lower part of the building
the latter part of the night
the last part of the night

tatpurusha.english_name: Accusative Tatpurusha
tatpurusha.rule: A word ending in the accusative (द्वितीया) case compounds with one of a closed list of past/present participial or desiderative uttarapadas: श्रित, अतीत, patita, gata, atyasta, प्राप्त, आपन्न (by सूत्र), extended by a वार्तिक to also cover gamya, गामिन्, and बुभुक्षु-type words. The uttarapada must be exactly one of this list — nothing else, however similar in sense, qualifies.
related_ashtadhyayi: वार्तिक: गम्यादीनाम् उपसंख्यानम् (extends the list to gamya/गामिन्/बुभुक्षु-type words)
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa — both members' case endings drop on समास
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book stresses the list is closed: 'अन्नं भुक्तवान्' (one who has eaten food) does NOT compound to 'अन्नभुक्तवान्', because भुक्तवान् is not on the श्रित-list, even though it looks structurally identical to the examples that do compound.

examples.gloss: one who has taken refuge in Krishna
one who has passed beyond sorrow
one who goes to the village
one who goes to the city

tatpurusha.english_name: Instrumental Tatpurusha — with comparison/deficiency/quarrel words
tatpurusha.rule: A word ending in the instrumental (तृतीया) case compounds with one of: पूर्व, सदृश, sama, ऊनार्थ (words meaning 'deficient by'), kalaha, निपुण, मिश्र, संमिश्र, श्लक्ष्ण, avara.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

examples.gloss: deficient by a माष (a weight unit)

tatpurusha.english_name: Instrumental Tatpurusha — with a participial (कृत्-formed) second member
tatpurusha.rule: An instrumental-ending word compounds, generally (प्रायः — not invariably), with a कृदन्त (participle) as either its agent (कर्तृ) or its instrument (करण).
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The सूत्र's own word 'bahulam' (generally/not invariably) is illustrated by a negative example: 'दण्डेन ताडितवान्' does NOT compound to 'दण्डताडितवान्', despite matching the pattern of the other examples.

tatpurusha.english_name: Instrumental Tatpurusha — a food seasoned by, or a food mixed with, another
tatpurusha.rule: Two related rules: a food-word (अन्नवाचिन्, e.g. rice) compounds with an instrumental word denoting the substance it is prepared/seasoned with (curd, milk); and an edible-word (भक्ष्यवाचिन्) compounds with an instrumental word denoting what is mixed into it (jaggery etc.).
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

tatpurusha.english_name: Dative Tatpurusha
tatpurusha.rule: A dative-ending word compounds with one of six words: tadartha ('that for which' — used only where a raw material becomes a product, प्रकृतिविकृतिभाव), artha (this compound is obligatory/nitya, and the whole compound takes the gender of the qualified noun rather than artha's own), bali, hita, sukha, रक्षित.
related_ashtadhyayi: वार्तिक: arthena नित्यसमासो विशेष्यलिङ्गता ceti vaktavyam
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book explicitly warns that beyond these six words, a dative-ending word does NOT compound with anything else (rare प्रकृतिविकृति exceptions aside). It gives 'गुरुदक्षिणा' as a trap: this looks like it could be चतुर्थीतत्पुरुष ('gurave दक्षिणा') but its real vigraha is genitive — 'गुरोः दक्षिणा' (i.e. it is a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, see tatpurusha-6).

examples.gloss: gold meant for an earring (tadartha: gold=raw material, earring=product)
wood meant for a sacrificial post
this (soup), meant for a brahmin — masculine to agree with सूपः
this (gruel), meant for a student — feminine to agree with यवागूः
this (milk), meant for an infant — neuter to agree with पयः

tatpurusha.english_name: Ablative Tatpurusha — fear/dread from something
tatpurusha.rule: An ablative-ending word compounds with bhaya, भीत, भीति, or भी (all meaning fear/afraid) as uttarapada.
related_ashtadhyayi: वार्तिक: भयभीतभीतिभीभिर् iti वाच्यम् (extends bhayena to the भीत/भीति/भी word-forms too)
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: Only bhaya/भीत/भीति/भी qualify — 'चोराद् रक्षितः' and 'व्याघ्रात् त्रातः' do NOT compound despite the parallel sense. The commentators (भाष्यकार) do however allow two further exceptions outside this word-list: 'ग्रामान् निर्गतः → ग्रामनिर्गतः' and 'अधर्माद् जुगुप्सुः → अधर्मजुगुप्सुः'.

tatpurusha.english_name: Ablative Tatpurusha — separated/fallen/freed from something
tatpurusha.rule: A small, closed set of ablative-ending words compound with apeta, अपोढ, mukta, patita, or apatrasta as uttarapada.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The सूत्र's own word 'अल्पशः' (sparingly) signals this compound is not fully general even within the five listed words: the book notes 'प्रासादात् पतितः' does NOT compound to 'प्रासादपतितः', and that whether the compound applies has to be checked against actual attested (शिष्ट-prayoga) usage rather than assumed.

tatpurusha.english_name: Ablative Tatpurusha — 'beyond a hundred/thousand' (irregular word order)
tatpurusha.rule: An ablative-ending शत (hundred) or sahasra (thousand) compounds with para ('beyond'), by a वार्तिक. Unusually, this pair is listed among the irregularly-formed (निपातन) compounds of the राजदन्तगण, so the normal word order is reversed — para is placed first — with a सुट् augment.
tatpurusha.ashtadhyayi_ref: वार्तिक under 2.1.37-38 (governed as part of the राजदन्तगण निपातन list)
tatpurusha.process: निपातन (irregular fixed listing) — uttarapada para placed before पूर्वपद, with सुट् augment

tatpurusha.english_name: Genitive Tatpurusha
tatpurusha.rule: A genitive-ending word compounds with a following subanta — the broadest and least restricted of the seven vibhakti-तत्पुरुषस्, with two general caveats: a genitive expressing mere 'quality' (गुणार्थ) does not usually compound (though the book notes rare exceptions), and a genitive-form indeclinable does not compound unless it is itself krit-formed.
related_ashtadhyayi: 5.4.91 राजाहःसखिभ्यष्टच् (समासान्त टच्-pratyaya after राजन्/ahan/sakhi in such compounds, e.g. राजधुरा)
5.4.74 ऋक्पूरब्ध्वः पथामानक्षे (accha-pratyaya for pathin- compounds, e.g. tripatham)
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa (plus समासान्त suffixes टच्/accha in specific listed words)

examples.gloss: a threefold road (a crossing of three roads)
a text first expounded by Panini
the shade of sugarcane (neuter, since not from over-abundance of the पूर्वपद — see book's own footnote contrast with वृक्षच्छाया)

tatpurusha.english_name: Locative Tatpurusha — expert/devoted/fixed 'in' something
tatpurusha.rule: A locative-ending word compounds with one of: शौण्ड, adhi, धूर्त, kitava, प्रवीण, पण्डित, कुशल, निपुण, capala, siddha, शुष्क, pakva, bandha.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

tatpurusha.iast_name: सप्तमीतत्पुरुषः (with ध्वाङ्क्ष, in a pejorative sense)
tatpurusha.english_name: Locative Tatpurusha — 'a crow at/in' (idiom of contempt)
tatpurusha.rule: A locative-ending word compounds with ध्वाङ्क्ष ('crow') as uttarapada only when a sense of censure/contempt (निन्दा) is intended — the compound is a figure of speech, not a literal statement about a crow.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

examples.gloss: 'a crow at the holy-bathing-place' — idiom for one who never stays long in gurukula-like places (guru-कुलेषु यः चिरं na vasati सः)
same idiom, with काक in place of ध्वाङ्क्ष

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — adjective as first member (general)
tatpurusha.rule: General definition of karmadharaya: a tatpurusha where both members stand in the same case (समानाधिकरण). This base case: a word denoting a quality (विशेषण) compounds, generally (bahulam), with the noun it qualifies (विशेष्य), the adjective coming first.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; पूर्वपद order is fixed — the book notes the adjective must come first even if the vigraha places it second (e.g. 'वैयाकरणः प्रथमः' still gives 'प्रथमवैयाकरणः', not 'वैयाकरणप्रथमः')

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — with 'former-time', eka, sarva, jarat, पुराण, nava, kevala
tatpurusha.rule: Same-case compounding of eka, sarva, jarat, पुराण, nava, kevala with the noun they qualify; also पूर्व when used in a 'former-time' (पूर्वकाल) sense, e.g. denoting one action preceding another.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

examples.gloss: one who bathed and then was anointed — पूर्व used in its 'former-in-time' sense, not appearing overtly in the compound

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — with पूर्व, apara, prathama, carama, jaghanya, समान, madhya, madhyama, वीर
tatpurusha.rule: Same-case compounding of पूर्व ('former'), apara ('other/latter'), prathama ('first'), carama ('last'), jaghanya ('lowest'), समान ('same'), madhya/madhyama ('middle'), वीर ('heroic') with the noun they qualify. A वार्तिक notes that when apara means 'later' (in time), it takes the form पश्चात् instead.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

examples.gloss: the latter half — apara in its 'later' sense surfaces as पश्चात्

tatpurusha.iast_name: विशेषणपूर्वपदः (with sat/mahat/parama/uttama/उत्कृष्ट, before an honored referent)
tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — with sat, mahat, parama, uttama, उत्कृष्ट, qualifying something respected
tatpurusha.rule: Same-case compounding of sat ('good'), mahat ('great'), parama ('supreme'), uttama ('best'), उत्कृष्ट ('excellent') with a noun that denotes something honored/respected (पूज्यमान).
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

examples.gloss: the best person / first grammatical person

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — a direction- or number-word compounding to form a fixed name
tatpurusha.rule: A direction-word (dik) or number-word (सङ्ख्या) compounds with a same-case noun specifically when the result denotes a proper name/fixed designation (संज्ञा) — not a mere count. The book cautions this is why 'षड्भिः मन्त्रैः' stays uncompounded (a genuine instrumental count) while 'सप्तर्षयः' compounds (a fixed name, 'the Seven Sages').
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book adds that later usage ('navarasaciram', 'त्रिलोकनाथेन', 'षोडशपदार्थानाम्') shows सङ्ख्यावाची words compounding even outside the strict संज्ञा case — but only when the phrase itself is treated as denoting a fixed set (e.g. नवसंख्याका रसाः = 'the nine rasas' as a known set), which is really the madhyamapadalopa mechanism (karmadharaya-12) supplying the missing middle word.

examples.gloss: five mango trees (as a named/counted set)

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — adjective as second member
tatpurusha.rule: Two related rules place the adjective last instead of first: (1) something being disparaged (कुत्स्यमान) compounds with a disparaging word (kutsana); (2) a class/kind-word (जाति) compounds with a word of praise (प्रशंसा).
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; uttarapada order reversed from the default विशेषणपूर्वपद pattern
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: One example in the source, 'पुरुषः प्रशस्तः = पुरुषमचर्चिका', uses a word (मचर्चिका) whose reading in the scan is uncertain — reproduced here as printed but flagged rather than glossed with invented confidence.

examples.gloss: a Mimamsaka, disparaged as a दुर्दुरूट

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — both members adjectival (a thing described positively and negatively)
tatpurusha.rule: A past-participle (kta-anta) not itself negated compounds with the corresponding negated (नञ्विशिष्ट) past-participle of the same root, expressing 'done and not done' style pairs.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — the standard of comparison first
tatpurusha.rule: A word denoting the standard of comparison (उपमान) compounds with a word denoting the common property (सामान्यवचन), the उपमान coming first.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; iva ('like') in the vigraha does not surface in the compound

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — the standard of comparison last
tatpurusha.rule: The thing being compared (upameya) compounds with an उपमान word from the व्याघ्रगण (a listed set: व्याघ्र, सिंह, ऋक्ष, ऋषभ, hastin, पुण्डरीक, बलाहक, etc.), but only when the shared property (साधारण-dharma) is NOT separately stated in the sentence. A related rule extends the same pattern with वृन्दारक, नाग, कुञ्जर for something being honored/eminent.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The 'no shared-property word' condition is illustrated by contrast: 'पुरुषः व्याघ्रः iva' compounds to 'पुरुषव्याघ्रः', but if one wants to additionally say 'शूरः' (brave) — 'पुरुषो व्याघ्र iva शूरः' — the compound must NOT be made, precisely because साधारण-dharma (शूरः) is now stated.

examples.gloss: a bull of a man / a foremost man
a king who is like Indra

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — emphatic 'indeed/only' sense
tatpurusha.rule: A विशेषणविशेष्य compound (same general rule as karmadharaya-1) where the vigraha carries an emphatic eva ('indeed/only') right after the adjective, to show that the first member IS essentially the second, rather than merely qualifying it. The eva itself does not appear in the compound.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; the eva of the vigraha is silent in the compound

examples.gloss: the teacher, who IS (like) a god

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — 'so-called' sense (a proper name plus its category)
tatpurusha.rule: Same general विशेषणविशेष्य rule, applied when the 'adjective' is itself a proper name (संज्ञाशब्द), with the vigraha placing 'iti' ('called/named') right after it. Like the eva of अवधारणा, the iti does not appear in the compound.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; the iti of the vigraha is silent in the compound

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — elision of the middle word
tatpurusha.rule: Same विशेषणविशेष्य rule, but here the 'adjective' member is itself already a full compound at the vigraha stage; when that compound becomes the qualifier, its own second member (the word standing in the middle of the eventual three-word sense) is dropped. Named for this reason 'madhyamapada-lopa'.
tatpurusha.process: the vigraha involves three words; the middle one is elided on forming the compound
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book flags that 'द्विशतम्' is genuinely ambiguous between 102 (द्व्यधिकं शतम्, '2 added to 100') and 200 (द्विगुणितं शतम्, '100 doubled') — both routes independently elide a middle word down to the same surface form, so context alone disambiguates.

examples.gloss: a king (fond of vegetables) — 'प्रियः' (fond of), the middle word, is dropped
a brahmin (who worships the gods) — 'पूजकः' dropped
200 — '100 doubled' — same surface form as above, disambiguated by context

tatpurusha.english_name: Karmadharaya — the मयूरव्यंसक irregulars-list
tatpurusha.rule: A closed, irregularly-listed (निपातन) set of compounds whose formation is not derivable from any of the general karmadharaya rules above; the काशिका comments that any tatpurusha lacking a stated general rule (avihita-लक्षण) is to be looked for in this गण.
tatpurusha.process: निपातन — irregular, listed forms, not derived by a general productive rule

tatpurusha.english_name: Dvigu — in a taddhita-suffix sense (typically 'offspring of N mothers/fathers')
tatpurusha.rule: A number-word compounds with a following subanta in a sense that would otherwise require a secondary (taddhita) derivative suffix — most often the 'child of N [parents/mothers]' sense, or 'prepared using N [items]'.
tatpurusha.ashtadhyayi_ref: 2.1.51 (base dvigu-formation sutra, shared by all three dvigu subtypes below)
related_ashtadhyayi: 2.1.52 संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः (defines the name 'dvigu' itself: a number-word-first compound)
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; the sense is that of an unexpressed taddhita suffix

examples.gloss: offspring of two mothers (a well-known epithet of Ganesha)
an oblation-cake prepared in five potsherds

tatpurusha.english_name: Dvigu — functioning as the first member of a further (bahuvrihi-like) compound
tatpurusha.rule: A dvigu compound itself becomes the पूर्वपद of a larger compound, the whole then describing someone who possesses that many of the thing named (a बहुव्रीहि sense built on top of a dvigu).
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa, then the resulting dvigu itself serves as पूर्वपद of an outer possessive (बहुव्रीहि-sense) compound

examples.sandhi: पञ्च गावः धनं यस्य सः = पञ्चगवधनः
examples.iast: पञ्च गावः धनं yasya सः = पञ्चगवधनः

examples.iast: दश गावः धनं yasya सः = दशगवधनः

tatpurusha.english_name: Dvigu — collective sense ('a group of N')
tatpurusha.rule: A number-word compounds with a noun to denote a collection (समाहार) of that many members, treated as one unit. Such a compound is always singular in number, regardless of the count named.
tatpurusha.process: vibhakti-lopa; obligatorily singular regardless of the number named
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book gives detailed gender rules for समाहार-dvigu, condensed here: (i) it is neuter by default (समाहारे द्विगुः द्वन्द्वः ca नपुंसकलिङ्गं स्यात्, 2.4.17); (ii) EXCEPT that ahan ('day') as uttarapada keeps masculine gender (रात्राहाहाः पुंसि, 2.4.21), as in सप्ताहः, द्व्यहः; (iii) an a-ending uttarapada elsewhere often shifts to ई-ending feminine (a वार्तिक + 4.1.21 द्विगोः), as in त्रिलोकी, पञ्चवटी — EXCEPT words in the पात्र/bhuvana/yuga-गण, which stay neuter (पञ्चपात्रम्, tribhuvanam, caturyugam); (iv) रात्रि ('night') as uttarapada becomes a-ending in the compound but stays neuter rather than becoming feminine, by a separate गणसूत्र (संख्यापूर्वं रात्रं क्लीबम्), as in dvyaham, cf. त्रिरात्रम्/पञ्चरात्रम्/नवरात्रम् which read as neuter -am forms despite रात्रि's own feminine gender outside compounds.

examples.gloss: a week (a group of seven days)
a grove of five banyan trees (Panchavati)

tatpurusha.english_name: Negative Tatpurusha — नञ् ('not') plus a noun
tatpurusha.rule: The negative particle नञ् (surfacing as a-/an-) obligatorily compounds with a following subanta.
tatpurusha.process: nitya-समास (obligatory); नञ् surfaces as an- before vowels, a- before consonants
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: Two cautions from the book: (1) in a phrase like 'avighnam astu' ('may there be no obstacle'), the vigraha is 'विघ्नानाम् अभावः' (the absence of obstacles) — an abstract sense that reclassifies the compound as अव्ययीभाव rather than नञ्तत्पुरुष. (2) नञ् and na are two distinct indeclinables with the same meaning; a handful of compounds like 'नैकधा' (not in one way) and 'नान्तरीयकम्' are formed with the plain word na, not with नञ् — the difference shows up in whether the n-sound itself undergoes further elision in the compound (it does under नञ्, not under na).

examples.gloss: not a (proper) road — an optional समासान्त suffix gives the second form, which then takes neuter gender

tatpurusha.english_name: Ku-Tatpurusha — 'bad/deficient' plus a noun
tatpurusha.rule: Ku ('bad, deficient, little') obligatorily compounds with a following subanta. Ku itself never occurs as an independent word, so its vigraha is always an aswapada-vigraha (paraphrased with unrelated words, not the compound's own members) — the same situation seen with upa-कृष्णम् earlier.
related_ashtadhyayi: 6.3.101 कोः कत्तत्पुरुषे'ci (kad-substitution before a vowel-initial uttarapada)
6.3.106 विभाषा पुरुषे (ku optionally becomes का before पुरुष)
tatpurusha.process: nitya-समास (obligatory), aswapada-vigraha; ku optionally substitutes as का before 'पुरुष', and as kad before a vowel-initial uttarapada

examples.gloss: a bad/cowardly man — का-form optional before पुरुष specifically
bad food — kad-form before the vowel-initial anna

tatpurusha.english_name: Gati-Tatpurusha — a word bearing the technical 'gati' designation, plus a कृत्-form
tatpurusha.rule: A word carrying पाणिनि's technical gati-संज्ञा (a closed, सूत्र-assigned label — not a natural-language category, and one the book says spans 'many सूत्रस्' it does not enumerate) obligatorily compounds with a following derived (typically कृदन्त, especially कृत्वा-absolutive) word. Every such compound has an aswapada-vigraha, since it is always obligatory (nitya).
tatpurusha.process: nitya-समास (obligatory), aswapada-vigraha
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book's own list here runs to roughly 20 examples across two pages; this is a representative selection, not the full list — the underlying gati word-set itself is large and सूत्र-defined rather than semantically predictable.

examples.gloss: having made (something) into a livelihood, as it were
having treated (something) as secret, like an Upanishad

tatpurusha.english_name: प्रादि-Tatpurusha — pra and 21 other prefixes, plus a noun
tatpurusha.rule: Any of a fixed set of 22 prefixes (प्रादयः — pra, परा, apa, sam, and others) obligatorily compounds with a following subanta. Always obligatory (nitya), hence aswapada-vigraha throughout.
tatpurusha.process: nitya-समास (obligatory), aswapada-vigraha
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book lists 22 prefixes and gives one example per prefix, running well beyond this selection; only a representative subset is included here.

tatpurusha.english_name: Upapada-Tatpurusha — a word bearing the technical 'upapada' designation, plus a कृत्-form (often an agent noun)
tatpurusha.rule: A word carrying पाणिनि's technical upapada-संज्ञा obligatorily compounds with a following derived word (very often a कृत्-formed agent noun in -a/-in etc., such as -कार, -bhojin, -याजिन्). Always obligatory, hence aswapada-vigraha.
tatpurusha.process: nitya-समास (obligatory), aswapada-vigraha; some forms show mum-आगम (e.g. प्रियंवदः) rather than the expected accusative alug
tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: The book's list runs to roughly 17 examples; a representative selection is included here.

bahuvrihi.english_name: Bahuvrihi — general (same-case members), a compound naming something else entirely
bahuvrihi.rule: Two or more subantas, generally in the same case, compound to name a third thing (anya-पदार्थ) that possesses what the compound describes — the compound's own members are not what is finally denoted. E.g. 'पीताम्बरः' does not mean 'yellow' or 'garment', it means 'one who wears a yellow garment' (Krishna/Vishnu).
bahuvrihi.process: vibhakti-lopa; the compound as a whole functions as an adjective describing a possessor, agreeing in gender/number/case with whatever it modifies (not fixed by its own members' original gender)

one by whom a vehicle has been mounted
one by whom a meal has been eaten

bahuvrihi.rule: Terminological distinction: when the two bahuvrihi members are in the SAME case, it is called समानाधिकरण (as in bahuvrihi-1); when they are in DIFFERENT cases (typically a locative पूर्वपद plus a nominative uttarapada), it is called व्यधिकरण.
bahuvrihi.process: vibhakti-lopa (usually) — but see flagged nuance for an exception

bahuvrihi.english_name: Bahuvrihi — a number-word as second member ('nearly/beyond N')
bahuvrihi.rule: Avyaya (indeclinable), आसन्न ('near'), अदूर ('not far'), or adhika ('more') compounds with a following number-word, in the sense of 'approximately/close to/beyond' that count. All resulting forms are obligatorily plural.
bahuvrihi.process: vibhakti-lopa; result always plural, regardless of the sense

bahuvrihi.english_name: Bahuvrihi — a number-word compounding with another number-word ('two or three')
bahuvrihi.rule: A number-word (in the sense of a countable quantity) compounds with another number-word, expressing 'this many or that many'.

bahuvrihi.rule: The word saha ('with') compounds with an instrumental-ending word, in the sense of accompaniment/possession. A related rule optionally simplifies saha itself to sa in the compound.
bahuvrihi.process: vibhakti-lopa; saha optionally simplifies to sa (a much shorter, very common form: sa-पुत्रः etc.)

bahuvrihi.rule: The word अविद्यमानम् ('non-existent') compounds with a following subanta; when the compound is formed, the word विद्यमान itself is elided, leaving only the negative prefix visible.

bahuvrihi.english_name: Bahuvrihi — a pra-class prefix plus a verb-derived nominative word
bahuvrihi.rule: A pra-class prefix-word (pra, nir, su, dur, etc.) compounds with a following verb-derived (धातुज) nominative word belonging to yet another nominative word; the verb-derived word's own uttarapada is then elided in the compound.
bahuvrihi.process: the vigraha's own middle verb-derived word (like gata-) is elided on forming the compound

bahuvrihi.english_name: Bahuvrihi — a comparison-word (उपमान) as first member
bahuvrihi.rule: Two related rules: (i) a compound that already contains a locative word plus an उपमान word further compounds with another word, dropping the middle uttarapada; (ii) a plain उपमान word alone compounds directly with any other subanta to describe a possessor with that comparison.

dvandva.rule: Two or more subantas joined by 'and' (ca) in the vigraha compound together, each retaining its own individual reference — the compound is dual or plural according to how many things are actually named, unlike समाहार-dvandva which collapses to singular.

dvandva.rule: The same word-pairs that could form an itaretara-dvandva may optionally instead form a collective (समाहार) compound, treating the pair/group as one unit; such compounds take neuter singular gender, per the same rule that governs collective dvigu compounds.

avyayibhava.english_name: Avyayibhava — indeclinable as first member (the main type, 20 senses)
avyayibhava.rule: An indeclinable (avyaya) compounds with a following subanta, the whole standing in one of some twenty listed senses (case-relation, nearness, prosperity, decline, absence, ending, unsuitability, sudden utterance, following, fitness, repetition, non-exceeding, similarity, sequence, simultaneity, attainment, entirety, inclusion-up-to, boundary-excluding, boundary-including, facing-towards). The whole compound is itself indeclinable, whatever the original members were.
avyayibhava.process: vibhakti-lopa; the whole compound becomes an indeclinable (avyaya), regardless of the original case of its uttarapada
avyayibhava.flagged_nuance: Senses 18 and 19 (मर्यादा 'boundary-excluding' vs abhividhi 'boundary-including') produce the identical surface compound 'आहिमालयम्' from the identical vigraha 'आ हिमालयात्' — the book uses this to illustrate that the same compound can denote 'China' (excluding the Himalayas) or 'India' (including them), purely by which sense is intended; the compound's form alone cannot disambiguate it.

purvapada_uttarapada_rules.note: Ch.3 of the source (pp.17-33) gives general and special morphological rules governing how the purvapada and uttarapada change shape on compounding (gender shifts, stem-final changes, samasanta suffixes), cutting across the samasa-type entries in the sections above rather than adding new compound types. Now complete for 3.1 (purvapada rules, general+special), 3.2 (uttarapada rules, general + special-by-samasa-class for tatpurusha/bahuvrihi/dvandva/avyayibhava), and 3.3 (a 5-rule gender-agreement summary). Ch.3 section 3.4 (esa sangrahah, pp.29-33) is a condensed recap table of the same rules already captured above with a handful of extra example words -- deliberately NOT duplicated here since it introduces no new rules.

purvapada_general.english_name: Sandhi is obligatory wherever it applies
purvapada_general.rule: Wherever an opportunity for phonological sandhi exists between the compound's members, sandhi must be applied — it is never left undone.
purvapada_general.process: standard sandhi rules apply across the compound boundary, same as anywhere else in a sentence

examples.gloss: the Lord's grace — derivation: bhagavat + anugraha → bhagavad + anugraha → भगवदनुग्रहः

purvapada_general.rule: If the पूर्वपद's प्रातिपदिक (nominal stem) ends in n, that n is dropped when the compound is formed.
purvapada_general.process: n-final stems (e.g. राजन्-) drop the final n before compounding

examples.gloss: the king's man — derivation: राजन् + पुरुष → राज + पुरुष → राजपुरुषः

purvapada_general.rule: In a नञ्-compound, the n-sound of नञ् itself (as opposed to the vowel a) is dropped.
purvapada_general.process: नञ् (n+a) loses its n, leaving just a- to prefix the uttarapada

examples.gloss: not righteousness — derivation: na (n+a) + dharma → a + dharma → अधर्मः

purvapada_general.english_name: The नुट् (n) augment before a vowel-initial uttarapada in नञ्-compounds
purvapada_general.rule: In a नञ्-compound, if the uttarapada begins with a vowel, then after the n of नञ् has already been dropped (per purvapada-general-3), an augment n (called नुट्) is inserted after the resulting a, to keep the two vowels from directly meeting.
purvapada_general.process: na (n+a) + vowel-initial word → a + word → a + n(नुट्) + word

examples.gloss: not the Lord/not capable — derivation: na (n+a) + ईश्वर → a + ईश्वर → a + n(नुट्) + ईश्वर → अनीश्वरः

purvapada_special.english_name: Masculine-like reversion of a feminine पूर्वपद
purvapada_special.rule: In karmadharaya and samanadhikarana-bahuvrihi, if the पूर्वपद is a feminine word that also has a common/masculine (भाषितपुंस्क, 'spoken-as-masculine') form available, it reverts to that masculine-like shape rather than keeping its own feminine ending.
purvapada_special.process: the feminine पूर्वपद's ending is replaced by the masculine-like (भाषितपुंस्क) stem before compounding

examples.gloss: a long rope — दीर्घा (fem.) reverts to दीर्घ- before compounding (cf. karmadharaya-1)
one whose wisdom is steady — स्थिता (fem.) reverts to sthita-

purvapada_special.rule: In karmadharaya and samanadhikarana-bahuvrihi, the पूर्वपद mahat ('great') has its final consonant t replaced by आ.

examples.gloss: one who has a great army — bahuvrihi, with पुंवद्भाव also applying to महती first

purvapada_special.english_name: The आनङ् substitute for ऋ-ending kinship words in dvandva
purvapada_special.rule: For ऋ-ending kinship words (मातृ, पितृ, etc.), the dvandva compound takes the substitute आनङ् (आ). This also applies when putra ('son') follows.
purvapada_special.process: मातृ/पितृ → माता/पिता (आ-substitution) before the dvandva's second member

purvapada_special.english_name: Lengthening of a vowel-ending पूर्वपद in कर्मव्यतिहार-bahuvrihi
purvapada_special.rule: In a karma-व्यतिहार-bahuvrihi (the reciprocal-action type, e.g. मुष्टामुष्टि), a vowel-ending पूर्वपद has its final vowel lengthened.
purvapada_special.process: final i/u etc. of the पूर्वपद is lengthened before the reduplicated uttarapada

examples.sandhi: मुष्ट्या मुष्ट्या प्रहत्य इदं युद्धं प्रवृत्तम् = मुष्टीमुष्टि
examples.iast: मुष्ट्या मुष्ट्या prahatya इदं युद्धं प्रवृत्तम् = मुष्टीमुष्टि
examples.gloss: a fist-fight — मुष्टि + मुष्टि → मुष्टी + मुष्टि (lengthened) → मुष्टीमुष्टि

uttarapada_general.english_name: pathin ('road') takes the samasanta suffix -a in any compound
uttarapada_general.rule: The word pathin, as uttarapada in any compound whatsoever, obligatorily takes the समासान्त suffix -a, becoming an a-ending stem (path-a-).

uttarapada_tatpurusha.rule: After sarva-, एकदेश- (i.e. पूर्व/apara/adhara/uttara/madhya/पश्चिम-type words), सङ्ख्यात-, पुण्य-, सङ्ख्या-, or avyaya-पूर्वपदस्, रात्रि obligatorily takes the समासान्त suffix -a (becoming a-ending). When it becomes a-ending this way, it also becomes masculine — except when preceded by a number-word, in which case it stays neuter instead. This rule does NOT apply to fixed compounds like शुभरात्रिः/शिवरात्रिः, which keep रात्रि as ई-ending feminine.
related_ashtadhyayi: 2.4.21 रात्राहाहाः पुंसि (रात्रि, ahan, अहः become masculine as a-ending समासान्त forms)
संख्यापूर्वं रात्रं क्लीबम् (a गणसूत्र: number-word + रात्र stays neuter)
uttarapada_tatpurusha.process: रात्रि + समासान्त -a → रात्र- (masculine, unless number-preceded, in which case neuter)

examples.gloss: the early part of the night
Navaratri — neuter here since number-preceded (cf. dvigu-3)
one that has gone past night

uttarapada_tatpurusha.english_name: राजन्, ahan, and sakhi take -a at the end of a tatpurusha
uttarapada_tatpurusha.rule: राजन् ('king'), ahan ('day'), and sakhi ('friend'), heard at the end of a tatpurusha, obligatorily take the समासान्त suffix -a, all three becoming a-ending stems.

uttarapada_tatpurusha.english_name: go ('cow') takes -a (masc.) / -ई (fem.) at the end of a tatpurusha
uttarapada_tatpurusha.rule: go, heard at the end of a tatpurusha, takes the समासान्त suffix -a: this yields an a-ending masculine stem, or an ई-ending feminine stem, according to the intended gender.

uttarapada_tatpurusha.english_name: nau ('boat') takes -a at the end of a dvigu or after ardha
uttarapada_tatpurusha.rule: nau, heard at the end of a dvigu compound, or right after ardha ('half'), obligatorily takes the समासान्त suffix -a, becoming an a-ending stem.

uttarapada_tatpurusha.english_name: Exceptions — when the tatpurusha samasanta suffix is blocked
uttarapada_tatpurusha.rule: Three contexts block the समासान्त suffix that would otherwise apply: (1) when su or ati is used in an honorific ('praising') sense before a word that would otherwise take a समासान्त suffix, that suffix is blocked; (2) when kim is used in a derogatory sense, the word following it is likewise blocked from taking the suffix; (3) a नञ्पूर्वपद tatpurusha never takes a समासान्त suffix at all — except pathin, which takes it optionally.
uttarapada_tatpurusha.sutra_devanagari: न पूजनात् / किमः क्षेपे / नञस्तत्पुरुषात् / पथो विभाषा
uttarapada_tatpurusha.sutra_iast: na पूजनात् / किमः क्षेपे / नञस् तत्पुरुषात् / patho विभाषा
uttarapada_tatpurusha.process: the समासान्त suffix that the uttarapada would otherwise take (e.g. राजन् → राज-) is blocked in these three contexts
uttarapada_tatpurusha.flagged_nuance: 'apatham' (neuter, with the suffix) is possible for pathin under नञ्, per the pathin-specific optionality — 2.4.30 अपथं नपुंसकम् confirms it takes neuter gender when the suffixed form is used.

examples.gloss: a good king — su in honorific sense blocks राज- suffixing, so राजा stays n-ending
an exceedingly great king — likewise blocked
a contemptible king — kim in derogatory sense blocks suffixing
no king — नञ् blocks suffixing entirely
not a (proper) road — pathin alone gets the optional suffixed form, apatham, which is then neuter

uttarapada_bahuvrihi.english_name: dharma takes the anic (-an) samasanta suffix in bahuvrihi
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.rule: dharma, at the end of a (non-compound-final-only, i.e. 'kevala') bahuvrihi, obligatorily takes the anic suffix, becoming an n-ending stem.

examples.gloss: one by whom dharma has been seen/realized

uttarapada_bahuvrihi.english_name: The reciprocal-action bahuvrihi takes -ic and becomes indeclinable
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.rule: The reciprocal-action (व्यतिहार) type of bahuvrihi obligatorily takes the ic suffix and, as a result, becomes an indeclinable.

examples.sandhi: दण्डैः दण्डैः प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं प्रवृत्तम् = दण्डादण्डि
examples.iast: दण्डैः दण्डैः प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं प्रवृत्तम् = दण्डादण्डि

uttarapada_bahuvrihi.english_name: dhanus takes अनङ्; जाया takes निङ्, in bahuvrihi
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.rule: dhanus ('bow'), at the end of a bahuvrihi, takes the substitute अनङ्, becoming n-ending. जाया ('wife'), at the end of a bahuvrihi, takes the substitute निङ्.
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.process: dhanus + अनङ् → dhanvan-; जाया + निङ् → जानि-

examples.gloss: one whose bow is the Gandiva (Arjuna)

uttarapada_bahuvrihi.english_name: gandha takes the it substitute in three distinct bahuvrihi contexts
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.rule: gandha ('smell') takes the substitute it in bahuvrihi in three separate contexts: (i) after ut, पूति, su, or surabhi; (ii) when used in an 'a little/faint' (alpa) sense; (iii) after an उपमान (comparison) word.

examples.gloss: food with a faint smell of ghee (alpa-)

examples.sandhi: मत्स्यगन्ध इव गन्धः यस्याः सा = मत्स्यगन्धिः
examples.iast: matsyagandha iva गन्धः यस्याः सा = मत्स्यगन्धिः

uttarapada_bahuvrihi.english_name: पाद loses its final a; feminine ई/ऊ/ऋ-ending and other 'remainder' words take -kap; आ-ending feminines and go shorten in bahuvrihi
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.rule: Several further bahuvrihi-specific stem changes: (1) पाद ('foot'), after a number-word or su-, loses its final a; (2) a feminine word ending in ई or ऊ, or a word ending in ऋ, at the end of a bahuvrihi, takes the kap suffix; (3) any other ('remaining', शिष्ट) word not covered by the rules above may optionally take kap at the end of a samanadhikarana-bahuvrihi; (4) a feminine आ-ending word, or go, shortens its final vowel at the end of a bahuvrihi — and when kap follows, the आ-ending feminine optionally stays short.
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.sutra_iast: संख्यासुपूर्वस्य / नद्युतश् ca / शेषाद् विभाषा / gostriyor upasarjanasya, आपो'न्यतरस्याम्
uttarapada_bahuvrihi.process: various — see rule field for each sub-case

examples.gloss: one who has two feet — final a lost after a number-word
one by whom a river has been crossed — ई-ending word takes kap

examples.sandhi: कठोरं चेतः यस्य सः = कठोरचेतस्कः / कठोरचेताः
examples.iast: कठोरं चेतः yasya सः = कठोरचेतस्कः / कठोरचेताः
examples.gloss: one whose heart is hard — a 'remaining' word, kap optional

examples.sandhi: अधीता विद्या येन सः = अधीतविद्यः / अधीतविद्यकः / अधीतविद्याकः
examples.iast: अधीता विद्या yena सः = अधीतविद्यः / अधीतविद्यकः / अधीतविद्याकः
examples.gloss: one by whom learning has been studied — आ-ending feminine, shortened, with optional kap and optional retention of आ before kap
one who has variegated cows — go shortens to -gu (cf. bahuvrihi-1)

uttarapada_dvandva.english_name: c-varga-, d-, ष्-, and h-final words take -a in samahara-dvandva
uttarapada_dvandva.rule: In a समाहार (collective) dvandva, an uttarapada ending in a c-class (palatal) consonant, or in d, ष्, or h, obligatorily takes the समासान्त suffix -a.

examples.sandhi: वाक् च त्वक् च अनयोः समाहारः = वाक्त्वचम्
examples.iast: वाक् ca tvak ca अनयोः समाहारः = वाक्त्वचम्
क्षत्रियाश् ca वणिजश् ca एतेषां समाहारः = क्षत्रियवणिजम्
sampac ca vipac ca अनयोः समाहारः = sampadvipadam

examples.sandhi: छत्रं च उपानत् च अनयोः समाहारः = छत्रोपानहम्
examples.iast: छत्रं ca उपानत् ca अनयोः समाहारः = छत्रोपानहम्

uttarapada_avyayibhava.english_name: How the final member of an avyayibhava behaves, by stem-ending
uttarapada_avyayibhava.rule: The uttarapada at the end of an avyayibhava behaves, in form, like the neuter singular of a fixed reference-word matching its own final sound: an a- or आ-ending word behaves like an a-ending neuter singular; an i- or ई-ending word behaves like वारि ('water'); a u-, ऊ-, o-, or au-ending word behaves like madhu ('honey'); an ऋ-ending word behaves like an ऋ-ending neuter singular. Whatever its original gender, the whole compound is always indeclinable.
uttarapada_avyayibhava.process: the final stem-vowel class determines which reference-paradigm the frozen singular form follows

examples.gloss: towards the one who does the work — ऋ-ending pattern

uttarapada_avyayibhava.english_name: An n-ending uttarapada takes -a in avyayibhava
uttarapada_avyayibhava.rule: An uttarapada ending in n, at the end of an avyayibhava, obligatorily takes the समासान्त suffix -a; if the sense is neuter, this is optional.
uttarapada_avyayibhava.process: n-final uttarapada + समासान्त -a → a-ending, following the same a-ending-neuter-singular behavior as uttarapada-avyayibhava-1

examples.gloss: according to the action — optional suffixing since the sense is neuter

gender_agreement_summary.english_name: Itaretara-dvandva and tatpurusha take the gender of the uttarapada
gender_agreement_summary.rule: Both itaretara-dvandva and tatpurusha (of any subtype) take whatever gender their final member (uttarapada) has.

examples.gloss: a bull and a buffalo-cow — dual, feminine ending (matching महिषी)
half a pause — masculine, matching विराम

gender_agreement_summary.rule: Both समाहार-dvandva and dvigu (of any subtype) take neuter gender by default (see dvigu-3 and dvandva-2/3 for the fuller set of exceptions to this default).

examples.sandhi: पाणी च पादौ च एतेषां समाहारः = पाणिपादम्
examples.iast: पाणी ca पादौ ca एतेषां समाहारः = पाणिपादम्

gender_agreement_summary.english_name: An a-ending uttarapada in dvigu becomes ई-ending feminine
gender_agreement_summary.rule: A dvigu compound whose uttarapada ends in a becomes feminine, shifting to an ई-ending stem — except for a short exempted list (पात्र, bhuvana, yuga-type words), which stay neuter.
gender_agreement_summary.process: a-ending uttarapada → ई-ending, feminine (exempting the पात्र/bhuvana/yuga-गण, cf. dvigu-3)

gender_agreement_summary.english_name: Bahuvrihi takes all three genders, agreeing with what it modifies
gender_agreement_summary.rule: A bahuvrihi compound is not fixed to any one gender by its own members — it takes masculine, feminine, or neuter freely, agreeing with whatever noun it describes.
gender_agreement_summary.process: compound gender = agrees with the modified noun, in all three genders

examples.gloss: a village that water has reached — masculine
a city (fem.) that water has reached — feminine
a town (neut.) that water has reached — neuter

gender_agreement_summary.rule: Every avyayibhava compound, whatever the gender of its own members, becomes an indeclinable (avyaya) as a whole.
gender_agreement_summary.process: compound becomes indeclinable regardless of original gender
